title: What are RS, angle R and angle S in the finished square?
description: In the square PQRS with a side of six centimetres, the length of RS and the angles at R and S are found from the two properties of a square. Keeko raises the doubt that the last two angles can be anything.
teaching_notes: One idea: a square always has equal sides and right angles, so the parts not yet drawn can be read off. Watch for children who think only the corners they drew are right angles.

source: In the square PQRS of side 6 cm just constructed, how long is the side RS and what are the measures of angle R and angle S?
video_script.why: The child uses the two properties of a square to read off the length of RS and the angles at R and S.
video_script.substitution: A square PQRS with a side of 6 cm, with right angles drawn at P and Q.
video_script.anchor: A square PQRS with a side of 6 cm, with the right angles at P and Q drawn and the corners R and S still to read
video_script.wrong_answer: the angles at the last two corners can be anything
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks the angles at the last two corners can be anything, as only two were drawn. The figure is a square, and a square has no corner that is not a right angle, so the bubble is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: R S is six centimetres, and the angles at R and S are both ninety degrees.

final_answer.value: RS = 6 cm, angle R = 90 degrees and angle S = 90 degrees
final_answer.spoken: R S is six centimetres, and the angles at R and S are both ninety degrees

never_show: the length of RS and the angles at R and S before the answer
maths_rules: Property S1: all 4 sides of a square are equal; property S2: all 4 angles are 90 degrees.
RS is a side of the square and PQ = 6 cm, so RS = 6 cm.
R and S are corners of the square, so angle R = 90 degrees and angle S = 90 degrees.
Check: PQ = QR = RS = SP = 6 cm.
video_script.design: One idea: the two properties of a square give the parts not yet drawn. Uses equal sides and right angles. Wrong idea: the last two angles can be anything. The square stays all video.
